chunks: When Our messages were read out to them, they said: 'We have heard. We could certainly compose (writings) like them if we choose. They are but only tales of long ago.'
ai.seo_question: How did the early disbelievers react when the Quran was recited to them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological arrogance of the Quraysh, who dismissed the Quran's eloquence as mere 'asatir' (tales of the ancients) to avoid acknowledging its divine source. Their claim of 'we could produce similar rhetoric' underscores the concept of i'jaz (inimitability), serving as a precursor to the challenge of producing a surah like it. This dismissal reflects a broader pattern of rejecting truth due to pride rather than intellectual deficiency.
